decision: scaffold first: npm, node>=24 running .ts directly, biome, strict tsc, node --test, ci, renovate
why: every later phase benefits from lint, typecheck and test gates existing before features

decision: ran three parallel architect runners (opus, sonnet, haiku) on the hunk-splitting data model and applier
why: the plan format and out-of-order hunk applier are one-way doors; want structurally distinct candidates before committing

decision: synthesized from opus and sonnet candidates: project file content from base plus applied change lines, no patch application at all
why: all hunks come from one diff so they are disjoint in base coordinates; out-of-order assignment cannot misapply, which deletes the fuzz matcher and its failure modes

decision: temporary index plus commit-tree with fixed dates instead of fast-import
why: same determinism, simpler to debug with ordinary git commands

decision: unanswered review comments are warnings, not validation errors
why: a human must still be able to apply a plan they are happy with

decision: mode-only text files get a TextFile with no hunks
why: the mode unit needs the base bytes to write the file; reusing TextFile keeps one projection path

decision: parseDiff also asserts that projecting every change line reproduces the tip blob
why: catches parser bugs at extract time, before a plan exists

decision: git diff runs with --no-abbrev and --no-textconv in addition to the contract flags
why: raw output abbreviates shas without --no-abbrev; textconv would make hunks disagree with blobs

decision: playback mode narrated by browser speech synthesis, narration text authored by the planner as optional plan fields
why: user wants to watch the branch being written with audio; built-in speech keeps it offline with no key or dependency, and putting narration in the plan keeps one source of truth per commit

decision: tree checks (path-conflict, final-mismatch) run only when the line assignment is complete
why: on a broken assignment they only restate unassigned and duplicate issues

decision: plan base mismatch is reported as malformed at $.base, tip mismatch as stale
why: the stale issue carries only the tip; a base mismatch means the plan was written for another merge-base

decision: two commands over one engine: split for the author (applies a branch, comments feed the next plan) and walk for a reviewer (no apply, playback with narration, comments become a markdown code review)
why: user clarified two personas; the projection, plan and review UI are shared, only the apply step and the feedback renderer differ

decision: commit-tree runs with --no-gpg-sign and messages get a trailing newline
why: commit.gpgSign would make SHAs non-deterministic and prompt for a key

decision: writeBranch returns unchanged when the ref already points at the computed head, even if expectedOld differs
why: the ref is already where apply would put it; refusing would break idempotent re-runs

decision: apply defaults --name to <branch>-split
why: never rewrites the user's branch unless asked; --name <branch> --force is safe because the final tree equals the checked-out tip

decision: issues and commit lists print 0-based commit indices
why: matches the $.commits[i] JSON paths the planner edits

decision: splitting is per change line, not per file or hunk; a plan takes any subset of a hunk's lines and orders lines of one file across commits freely
why: the user asked that lines move to an earlier commit when the story needs it; the projection engine already makes any line subset well-defined
result: confirmed, limit: no intermediate states absent from base or tip

decision: narration lives in the plan, on commits and on unit refs
why: one planner call produces both the commit order and the voice-over, and the narration stays bound to the exact units it describes
evidence: src/plan.ts parsePlanFile, src/anthropic.ts PLAN_SCHEMA, docs/DESIGN.md Reviewer mode and playback

decision: ran both flows by hand on the fixture: split (plan with a split hunk, check caught planted errors, apply proved the tree hash, v2 answered both comments) and walk (narrated plan, walk server, comment, code review digest)
why: prove it works on the real artifact, not the tests alone; the UI itself could not be opened because no browser is available on this machine
result: VERIFIED except the browser UI, INCONCLUSIVE there

decision: apply never writes the session's branch or any branch checked out in a worktree, --force included; supersedes the 04:27 entry that allowed --name <branch> --force
why: the user wants new commits on a new branch so the original is never at risk; update-ref on a checked-out branch desynchronises that worktree's index and files

decision: one review server per user that hosts many sessions; later review or walk calls register with it instead of starting another; busy port is probed for our own server first, otherwise a free port is chosen; uninstall mirrors install
why: user asked for a single server instance that still serves multiple repos and worktrees, graceful port handling, and easy uninstall

decision: apply, review and walk take <session>/lock; the lock is written whole to a temp file and link(2)ed into place, which fails on EEXIST like open(wx); a dead pid's lock is taken over; release removes the lock only if its token is ours
why: two agents on one session would otherwise race on freeze, applied.json and reviews/vN; link keeps a reader from seeing a half-written lock, which wx followed by write cannot; two processes breaking the same stale lock in the same instant can still both proceed

decision: clean removes sessions whose branch is gone, review drafts at or below the latest finished review version, locks and *.<pid>.*.tmp files of dead pids, and object quarantines of dead applies; plan versions are kept; --all removes .follow-me/ and refuses while a live process holds a session
why: a draft at or below the latest review can never be resumed because a version is reviewed once; temp names carry the pid so a live writer's file is never taken

decision: one review server per user: server.json in FOLLOW_ME_HOME, XDG_STATE_HOME/follow-me or ~/.local/state/follow-me, claimed by link like the session lock; a registry keyed by SessionId (12 hex of sha256 over the session dir) serves /s/<id>/; review and walk register with a live server or become it (foreground, or --detach as follow-me server run); the server takes the session lock over by token from the CLI; it exits 30s after its last session and removes server.json; supersedes the 06:36 plan
why: user asked for a single server instance that still handles many workstreams; a dir-derived id makes re-registering idempotent; taking the lock by token leaves no gap between CLI release and server acquire; the idle window lets back-to-back reviews reuse one server
evidence: src/server.ts startServer, src/host.ts, test/cli.test.ts two sessions share one server

decision: port handling: a --port held by our own server (GET /api/health answers app follow-me) means attach; held by anything else, listen on a free port and print 'port N is in use by another program, using M'; server stop only signals a pid that answers as ours on the recorded port
why: user asked that a taken port be handled gracefully; probing health rather than trusting the pid tells our server from a stranger and keeps a reused pid from being killed
evidence: src/host.ts startOrAttach and stopServer, test/cli.test.ts busy port tests

decision: linux-only test failures were EPIPE on git's stdin when git exited before reading it (optional ref lookups); handled on the stdin stream, ci green
why: the real git error already arrives through the exec callback, the pipe write failure was noise that only linux raised

decision: mermaid diagrams as a separate diagram field per commit and unit, rendered in a side panel that follows playback, mermaid bundled and served locally
why: user wants the agent to explain with diagrams during a walk; narration stays plain text because it is spoken; no cdn keeps the page offline

decision: apply signs split commits when git config --type=bool commit.gpgsign is true, --sign/--no-sign override; writeBranch passes -S or --no-gpg-sign explicitly; applied.json gains plan hash and signed, and apply skips the write and prints unchanged when version, hash, branch, signed and the branch head all match the record; supersedes the 04:23 --no-gpg-sign row
why: user needs signing preserved when recommitting; commit-tree is plumbing and ignores commit.gpgsign (git 2.9.1+), so not countermanding it would never sign; openpgp, x509 and ecdsa signatures differ per run so SHA equality cannot mean unchanged, while ed25519 is deterministic and still hits the SHA path
evidence: test/cli.test.ts ed25519 and ecdsa signing tests, git verify-commit on every split commit; disabling the record check fails the ecdsa test

decision: walk reviews and their autosaved drafts live in reviews/walk/vN.json (and vN.draft.json), chosen by host.ts loadHosted passing session.reviewsDir(mode) as Loaded.reviewsDir; reviews/vN.json stays the split slot, lastReview reads split only, older walk reviews in reviews/vN.json still count as walk reviews; asked for reviews/vN.walk.json
why: server.ts names both the review file and its draft from reviewsDir and the version, so a per-mode directory separates both without editing server.ts; a vN.walk.json name would still share vN.draft.json with a split review of the same plan
evidence: test/cli.test.ts walk after a split review of v1, feedback and feedback --walk print only their own comments; test/session.test.ts reviews and walkReviews
result: chosen; rename to vN.walk.json needs server.ts to take the file names from Loaded

decision: live loop: follow-me watch blocks until new comments, apply swaps the hosted plan version in place, the page re-renders on a server event and shows answers inline; ending the review stays optional
why: user does not want to close and reopen the server between plan versions; the server already hosts sessions and autosaves comments, so the missing pieces are a wait command, in-place version swap and page events
result: planned after the playback rebuild and the question loop

decision: the agent talks to the server api, not files: long-poll events endpoint with a sequence number, reply endpoint for explanations with optional mermaid, in-place version swap on apply; files remain the durable record written on end
why: user wants the loop to feel interactive; polling files is slow and racy, the server already owns the session state
result: planned, same slice as the live loop

decision: syntax highlighting in the review page from a locally served highlighter, language by file extension, diff state as background tint under token colours
why: user asked for highlighting while reviewing; a cdn would break the offline page

decision: every sliced commit must parse: prompt rule to keep files syntactically whole, a per-extension syntax gate in check and apply over projected files, --syntax override and --allow-syntax-errors escape
why: user wants intermediate commits syntactically correct even if they do not build; the projection makes each commit's file content available to parse without a checkout
result: planned after the live loop lands

decision: playback is the chunk stepper (Design B with C's context rules); a say step lasts the later of its reading time and speech end plus tail, for intros and chunks alike
why: the review lets a chunk reveal at speech end; taking the later of the two keeps a card readable when speech outruns reading at 1.5x and 2x, and one rule is simpler than two
evidence: test/playback.test.ts literal schedule at 1x and 2x; eight-commit fixture plays in 111.9s with speech at 1x (silent floor 108.5s), was 15.6s

decision: mermaid 12.2.0 exact-pinned; /vendor/mermaid.mjs serves dist/mermaid.esm.min.mjs and /vendor/chunks/mermaid.esm.min/<name>.mjs its chunks, names checked by regex; the page imports it dynamically only when a plan has a diagram and inserts its svg under securityLevel strict
why: the ESM build is split into about 200 chunks imported by relative path, so a single file cannot be served; dynamic import keeps diagram-free plans from loading it; strict mode has mermaid sanitize its own svg
evidence: src/server.test.ts fetches the entry and a chunk it imports; headless Chrome shows no /vendor request on a commit without a diagram

decision: gutter shows base and tip line numbers computed in the UI from hunk oldStart and earlier hunks of the file; comments display tip lines and removed lines by old number; anchors keep change indices
why: the review asked for real numbers without moving the comment wire format; the UI already has every hunk, so the server state needs nothing new
evidence: test/playback.test.ts lineNumbers and describeLines; fixture comment on mul's guards reads lines 14-15, matching git show feature:src/lib.js

decision: under 900px the rail hides titles visually (clip) rather than with display none, and its floating tooltip is described by aria-describedby; the index page's session age comes from an in-memory openedAt so HostedSummary and /api/sessions are unchanged
why: display none would drop the title from each row's accessible name; keeping age out of the summary avoids a wire change host.ts would have to parse
evidence: headless Chrome at 800px: row name keeps the title, tooltip shows on focus; server test asserts the index row and empty state

decision: dogfood: a naive one-commit-per-file planner so ci can run extract, check, apply and the proof on follow-me's own last commits; plus a hand-planned split of a real slice walked in the browser
why: user asked to dogfood on our own commits; real sources exercise the syntax gate and the projection better than the fixture

decision: record a playback gif for the readme after the chunk-stepper lands, via the preview browser recording and ffmpeg
why: user asked for a gif on github; recording before the pacing fix would show the wrong thing

decision: interactive loop: in-memory append-only event log per hosted session (long-poll and SSE), replies on comments, in-place version swap through the loader under the server's own lock, one renderReport for feedback, report and vN.md; check and apply validate against the open review's autosave
why: the owner wants agent and page to talk live without reopening the server; files stay the durable record; responses to comments that exist only on the open page must validate
evidence: server.test.ts events replies swap stream; cli.test.ts watch reply report apply swap; plan.test.ts concerns answers
result: chosen; open: no walk swap command, POST api/resolved is outside the contract, concern decisions have no undo route

decision: syntax gate by extension table: node --check for js, module.stripTypeScriptTypes in a child node for ts (node --check and --experimental-strip-types --check both reject valid ts, typescript 7 has no transpileModule), JSON.parse, sh/bash -n, py_compile; jsx tsx yaml and the rest skipped and counted; a file failing at the tip is the tip's own state and is not checked earlier; apply refuses unless --allow-syntax-errors
why: owner: sliced commits must stay syntactically correct but need not pass tests; blaming a split for a tip that does not parse would be wrong
evidence: node --check on ok.ts exits 1; stripTypeScriptTypes accepts it and rejects a missing brace; test/syntax.test.ts; scripts/dogfood.sh
result: chosen; open: yaml and jsx have no parser, tip failures warn instead of blocking, naive planner on a file-to-directory swap is untested
